title.zh: 卷398 列傳一百八十五 宗室祥厚 霍隆武 福珠洪阿 恩长 陈胜元 祁宿藻 陈克让 刘同缨 瑞昌 杰纯 锡龄阿
title.en: Volume 398 Biographies 185: Zong Shixianghou, Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong A, En Zhang, Chen Shengyuan, Qi Suzao, Chen Kerang, Liu Tongying, Rui Chang, Jie Chun, Xi Ling A
title.raw: 卷398 列傳一百八十五 宗室祥厚 霍隆武 福珠洪阿 恩长 陈胜元 祁宿藻 陈克让 刘同缨 瑞昌 杰纯 锡龄阿

sentences.zh: 列傳一百八十五

translations.literal: Biographies 185
translations.idiomatic: Biography 185

sentences.zh: 宗室祥厚霍隆武福珠洪阿恩長陳勝元祁宿藻陳克讓劉同纓

translations.literal: Imperial clansman Xianghou, Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong'a, En Chang, Chen Shengyuan, Qi Suzao, Chen Kerang, Liu Tongying
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansman Xianghou; Huo Longwu; Fu Zhu Hong'a; En Chang; Chen Shengyuan; Qi Suzao; Chen Kerang; Liu Tongying

sentences.zh: 瑞昌杰純錫齡阿

translations.literal: Rui Chang, Jie Chun, Xi Ling'a
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang; Jie Chun; Xi Ling'a

sentences.zh: 宗室祥厚，隸鑲紅旗，襲騎都尉世職，授鑾儀衛整儀尉。

translations.literal: The imperial clansman Xianghou belonged to the Bordered Red Banner, inherited the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and was appointed Ceremonial Guard orderly of the Imperial Procession.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou, a member of the imperial clan, was registered in the Bordered Red Banner. He inherited a hereditary commandant-of-cavalry post and was appointed an orderly in the Imperial Procession Guard.

sentences.zh: 累擢鑲紅旗蒙古副都統，歷山海關、熊岳、金州副都統。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Mongol Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Bordered Red Banner and served as deputy commander at Shanhaiguan, Xiongyue, and Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become Mongol deputy commander-in-chief of the Bordered Red Banner, and held deputy commandancies at Shanhaiguan, Xiongyue, and Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 道光二十八年，擢江寧將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Daoguang he was promoted to General of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1848 he was appointed general commanding the Jiangning garrison.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年正月，粵匪既陷武昌，兩江總督陸建瀛赴上游督師，祥厚偕江蘇巡撫楊文定留守江寧。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Xianfeng, after the Cantonese rebels had taken Wuchang, the Governor-General of the Two Jiangs Lu Jianying went upstream to direct the army; Xianghou, together with Jiangsu Governor Yang Wending, remained to hold Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1853, after the Taiping forces had captured Wuchang, Governor-General Lu Jianying of the Two Jiangs went upriver to take command of the campaign, while Xianghou and Jiangsu governor Yang Wending stayed behind to defend Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 賊已蔽江而下，壽春鎮總兵恩長戰歿，建瀛遽退，文定亦不候旨迳赴鎮江。

translations.literal: The rebels had already covered the river and come downstream; Shouchun garrison commander En Chang died in battle; Jianying abruptly withdrew, and Wending likewise went straight to Zhenjiang without awaiting imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were already sweeping down the Yangtze. Shouchun commander En Chang was killed in action. Jianying pulled back in haste, and Wending likewise rushed off to Zhenjiang without waiting for orders from the throne.

sentences.zh: 祥厚偕副都統霍隆武、提督福珠洪阿、布政使祁宿藻疏言：「督臣藉口江寧吃緊，趕回佈置，沿途險要，並不屯紮，上駛師船，一概撤回，專守水路之東西梁山。

translations.literal: Xianghou, together with Deputy Commander Huo Longwu, Regional Commander Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Provincial Administration Commissioner Qi Suzao memorialized, saying: "The Governor-General, citing the urgency at Jiangning, hurried back to make arrangements, yet at strategic points along the route he stationed no troops, recalled all war-junks going upstream, and devoted himself solely to guarding the Eastern and Western Liang hills on the water route.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou, Deputy Commander Huo Longwu, Regional Commander Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Provincial Commissioner Qi Suzao submitted a joint memorial: "The governor-general, pleading the crisis at Nanjing, hurried back to make dispositions; yet he left no garrisons at any of the strategic points along the way, recalled every war-junk that had been sent upriver, and concentrated his efforts only on holding the Eastern and Western Liang hills on the water route.

sentences.zh: 蕪湖為江蘇門戶，亦不設防。

translations.literal: Wuhu is the gateway to Jiangsu, yet no defense was set up there either.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhu, the gateway to Jiangsu, was left undefended as well.

sentences.zh: 十八日隻身抵省，遂致闔城驚擾。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth he arrived at the provincial capital alone, and the whole city was thrown into alarm.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighteenth he reached the capital by himself, throwing the entire city into panic.

sentences.zh: 臣等函勸速統舟師迎擊，乃督臣晏坐衙齋，三日不覆。

translations.literal: We wrote urging him to gather the fleet at once and meet the enemy; yet the Governor-General sat idle in his yamen and for three days gave no reply.
translations.idiomatic: We wrote urging him to assemble the fleet and strike the rebels at once, but the governor-general remained idle in his yamen and did not answer for three days.

sentences.zh: 撫臣執意移駐鎮江，挽留不顧，民情加倍驚惶。

translations.literal: The Governor was determined to move his headquarters to Zhenjiang and paid no heed to our pleas to stay; popular alarm was doubled.
translations.idiomatic: The governor insisted on shifting his headquarters to Zhenjiang and ignored our pleas to remain; public fear only grew worse.

sentences.zh: 自今固結民心，尚恐緩急難恃；

translations.literal: From this point, even if we now bind the people's hearts, we still fear they cannot be relied on in an emergency;
translations.idiomatic: Even if we rally the people now, we fear they will not stand by us when the crisis comes;

sentences.zh: 若任其紛紛遷徙，土匪因而竊發，奸細尤易勾結。

translations.literal: if they are allowed to scatter in flight, local bandits will seize the chance to rise, and enemy agents will find it all the easier to collude.
translations.idiomatic: and if the populace is allowed to flee in disorder, local bandits will rise in the confusion and enemy agents will find it all the easier to collude with them.

sentences.zh: 是未禦外侮，將成內變。

translations.literal: Thus before we have repelled the foreign foe, an internal upheaval will take shape.
translations.idiomatic: We shall face internal disorder before we have even repelled the invader.

sentences.zh: 現在督撫臣首鼠兩端，進退無據，以致省城震動。

translations.literal: At present the Governor-General and Governor are irresolute, with no firm ground for advance or retreat, so that the provincial capital is shaken.
translations.idiomatic: At present the governor-general and governor waver and cannot decide whether to advance or withdraw, and the provincial capital is in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 雖有旗兵志切同仇，無如兵力太單。

translations.literal: Although the banner troops are eager for revenge, there is no help for it that our forces are too few.
translations.idiomatic: Though the banner garrison is eager to fight, our numbers are far too few.

sentences.zh: 賊船順流下竄，朝發夕至，守禦萬分緊迫，督同道府等官及八旗協領，激勵官兵，安慰居民，竭盡血誠，認真辦理。

translations.literal: The rebel ships are fleeing downstream; they may set out in the morning and arrive by evening—the defense is desperately urgent. We, together with the circuit intendants, prefects, and other officials and the Eight Banners assistant commanders, are rousing the officers and troops, reassuring the inhabitants, and doing our utmost in all sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel fleet is racing downstream and may reach us overnight. The defense is desperately urgent. We, together with the circuit intendants, prefects, and Eight Banners assistant commanders, are doing all we can to hearten the troops, reassure the people, and carry out the defense in earnest.

sentences.zh: 請飭琦善、陳金綬迅速繞出賊前，協力堵剿，以固省城根本，維持南北大局。

translations.literal: We beg that Qi Shan and Chen Jinshou be ordered to move swiftly ahead of the rebels and join in blocking and suppressing them, to secure the foundation of the provincial capital and uphold the great balance of North and South.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that Qi Shan and Chen Jinshou be ordered to get ahead of the rebels at once and join in blocking and destroying them, to secure Nanjing and uphold the balance of power between north and south.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，詔逮建瀛治罪，命祥厚兼署總督，與霍隆武、福珠洪阿、祁宿藻悉心防禦，以在籍前廣西巡撫鄒鳴鶴熟悉賊情，命同籌辦。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was received, an edict ordered Jianying arrested and punished; Xianghou was ordered to act concurrently as Governor-General and, with Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Qi Suzao, to devote themselves to defense; and Zou Minghe, former Governor of Guangxi now at home and familiar with the rebels, was ordered to assist in planning.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, an edict ordered Jianying arrested and punished. Xianghou was appointed acting governor-general and, with Huo Longwu, Fu Zhu Hong'a, and Qi Suzao, charged to organize the defense. Zou Minghe, the former Guangxi governor now at home and familiar with the rebels, was ordered to assist in planning.

sentences.zh: 江寧城周九十六里，合旗、漢兵僅五千，城外江寧鎮、龍江關、上河分駐鄉勇不及三千，臨時召募，皆不足恃。

translations.literal: The Jiangning city wall measured ninety-six li in circumference; banner and Han troops together numbered only five thousand; outside the city, militia stationed at Jiangning town, Longjiang Pass, and Shanghe totaled fewer than three thousand; those recruited on the spot were all unreliable.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's walls ran ninety-six li around the circuit. Banner and Han troops together numbered only five thousand. Militia posted outside at Jiangning town, Longjiang Pass, and Shanghe came to fewer than three thousand, and men recruited at the last moment could not be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 賊過蕪湖，福山鎮總兵陳勝元率舟師戰歿，遂無御者，長驅直抵城下，四面環攻。

translations.literal: After the rebels passed Wuhu, Fushan garrison commander Chen Shengyuan led the fleet into battle and died; there was then no one to oppose them, and they drove straight to the foot of the walls and attacked on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels passed Wuhu, Fushan commander Chen Shengyuan led the river fleet into battle and was killed. With no one left to stop them, the rebels marched straight to the city and attacked on every side.

sentences.zh: 守逾旬，賊於儀鳳門穴地轟城，傾十餘丈，復由水西門、旱西門、南門緣梯而登，城遂陷。

translations.literal: The defense lasted more than ten days; the rebels at Yifeng Gate tunneled and blasted the wall, toppling more than ten zhang; they then scaled the wall by ladders at the Water West Gate, Dry West Gate, and South Gate, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: The defense held for more than ten days. At Yifeng Gate the rebels mined under the wall and blew a breach more than ten zhang wide, then scaled the ramparts by ladder at the Water West, Dry West, and South gates. The outer city fell.

sentences.zh: 祥厚偕霍隆武斂兵守駐防城，婦女皆助戰，逾日亦陷。

translations.literal: Xianghou, with Huo Longwu, gathered the troops to hold the garrison quarter; women also joined the fighting; after another day that too fell.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou and Huo Longwu drew their forces back into the banner garrison quarter. Women joined the fighting as well. A day later that stronghold too was lost.

sentences.zh: 祥厚手刃數賊，身被數十創，死之。

translations.literal: Xianghou killed several rebels with his own hand, received dozens of wounds, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou killed several rebels with his own blade, took dozens of wounds, and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太子太保，予二等輕車都尉世職，諡忠勇。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-rank Commandant of Light Chariots, and given the posthumous title Zhongyong (Loyal and Brave).
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-rank commandant-of-light-chariots title, and honored with the posthumous name Loyal and Brave.

sentences.zh: 入祀京師昭忠祠，於江寧建專祠，死事者附祀焉。

translations.literal: He was entered in the Zhaozhong Shrine in the capital; a special shrine was built for him at Jiangning, and those who died in the same cause were attached in worship.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the Zhaozhong Memorial Hall in Beijing, and a dedicated shrine was built for him at Nanjing, with others who died in the defense worshipped there as well.

sentences.zh: 霍隆武，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，福州駐防。

translations.literal: Huo Longwu, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, garrisoned at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Longwu, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner stationed at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 由武舉前鋒校歷官福建水師旗營協領。

translations.literal: From military licentiate and vanguard captain he rose through office to assistant commander of the Fujian naval banner camp.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen from military licentiate and vanguard captain to assistant commander of the Fujian naval banner camp.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，擢江寧副都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Deputy Commander of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was appointed deputy commander at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 賊圍城，偕祥厚登陴固守，歷十餘晝夜，外城陷，同守內城，策馬督戰，受傷墮，力竭陣亡，贈都統，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡果毅。

translations.literal: When the rebels besieged the city, he joined Xianghou on the ramparts in a stubborn defense for more than ten days and nights; when the outer city fell, they held the inner city together; he spurred his horse to direct the fighting, was wounded and fell, and died in battle when his strength was spent; he was posthumously made Commander-in-Chief, granted a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry with an additional Cloud Cavalry commandant, and given the posthumous title Guoyi (Resolute).
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels besieged the city, he and Xianghou held the ramparts for more than ten days and nights. After the outer city fell they defended the inner quarter together. He rode out to direct the fighting, was wounded and thrown from his horse, and died when his strength gave out. He was posthumously made commander-in-chief, granted a hereditary cavalry command with an additional cloud-cavalry title, and honored as Resolute.

sentences.zh: 當時駐防旗兵戰最力。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison banner troops fought with the greatest vigor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the garrison banner troops fought harder than anyone.

sentences.zh: 錫齡額者，事母孝，將軍本智異之，擢為參領。

translations.literal: Xi Ling'e was filial to his mother; General Benzhi took note of this and promoted him to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Ling'e was devoted to his mother. General Benzhi took notice and promoted him to company commander.

sentences.zh: 曰：「求忠臣必於孝子之門。

translations.literal: He said: "Seek loyal ministers at the door of filial sons."
translations.idiomatic: He remarked, "If you want a loyal minister, look among filial sons."

sentences.zh: 」事急，戒其妻：「國家豢養，無所報；

translations.literal: " When the crisis came, he warned his wife: "The state has fed and clothed us, and we have nothing with which to repay it;
translations.idiomatic: " When the crisis came he warned his wife: "The state has supported us, and we have done nothing to repay it.

sentences.zh: 脫不利，當闔門死。

translations.literal: if things go ill, the whole household must die together."
translations.idiomatic: If fortune turns against us, the whole household must die together."

sentences.zh: 」自守城，即不返家，舉室皆殉。

translations.literal: " From the day he took up the defense he did not return home, and the entire family perished with him.
translations.idiomatic: " From the day the siege began he never went home again, and his whole family died with him.

sentences.zh: 炳元，官佐領，勇力冠軍。

translations.literal: Bingyuan, an assistant company commander, was foremost in courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Bingyuan, an assistant company commander, was the strongest fighter in the garrison.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳門之陷，率死士奮鬥，賊為之卻，忽有狙擊者，殞於陣。

translations.literal: When Yifeng Gate fell, he led dare-to-die troops in fierce fighting and drove the rebels back, but suddenly a sniper struck and he fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: When Yifeng Gate was breached, he led a band of die-hards in a fierce counterattack and drove the rebels back, until a sniper's shot killed him on the field.

sentences.zh: 賊破內城，屠戮尤慘，男婦幾無孑遺。

translations.literal: When the rebels broke the inner city, the slaughter was especially dreadful; scarcely a man or woman was left alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels took the inner quarter the slaughter was especially dreadful; almost no one, man or woman, was left alive.

sentences.zh: 福珠洪阿，蘇完瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人，副都統佛安子。

translations.literal: Fu Zhu Hong'a, of the Suwan Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and son of Deputy Commander Fu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhu Hong'a, of the Suwan Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and the son of Deputy Commander Fu'an.

sentences.zh: 由鑾儀衛整儀尉累擢總兵，歷鎮筸、伊犁、西寧、天津諸鎮。

translations.literal: From Ceremonial Guard orderly he was promoted in succession to regional commander and served as garrison commander at Zhenqian, Ili, Xining, Tianjin, and other posts.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from an orderly in the Imperial Procession Guard to regional commander, commanding garrisons at Zhenqian, Ili, Xining, Tianjin, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 道光末，授江南提督，調陝西。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daoguang reign he was made Regional Commander of Jiangnan and then transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daoguang reign he was appointed regional commander of Jiangnan, then transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 粵匪起，江南籌防，仍調回舊任，駐守省城，所部兵僅數百人。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese rebels rose, Jiangnan made preparations for defense and he was transferred back to his former post, garrisoning the provincial capital with only a few hundred men under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion broke out, Jiangnan mobilized for defense and he was sent back to his old post at the provincial capital with only a few hundred men under his command.

sentences.zh: 地雷發，迎擊於城缺，斬悍賊，而諸門先後破。

translations.literal: When the mine exploded, he met the enemy at the breach and slew fierce rebels, but the gates fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When the mine blew open the wall he met the enemy at the breach and killed several of their best fighters, but the gates fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 賊四面至，往來巷戰，死之。

translations.literal: Rebels came from all sides; he fought back and forth in the lanes and died.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels poured in from every direction. He fought street by street through the lanes until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，予二等輕車都尉世職，諡壯敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-rank Commandant of Light Chariots, and given the posthumous title Zhuangmin (Stalwart and Keen).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-rank commandant-of-light-chariots title, and honored with the posthumous name Stalwart and Keen.

sentences.zh: 恩長，赫舍里氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: En Chang, of the Heseri clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: En Chang, of the Heseri clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 由親軍、十五善射，累遷安徽寧國營副將。

translations.literal: From imperial guardsman and one of the Fifteen Master Archers he was promoted in succession to brigade vice-commander of the Ningguo garrison in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as an imperial guardsman and as one of the Fifteen Master Archers before rising to brigade vice-commander of the Ningguo garrison in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光中治江防，被獎。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang period he managed river defense and was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign he managed river defenses and was commended for his work.

sentences.zh: 累擢壽春鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to garrison commander of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to commander of the Shouchun garrison.

sentences.zh: 初率兵守安慶，陸建瀛赴九江上游，調充翼長，為軍鋒。

translations.literal: At first he led troops to hold Anqing; when Lu Jianying went to the upper reaches at Jiujiang, En was transferred to serve as wing commander and spearhead of the army.
translations.idiomatic: At first he held Anqing with his troops. When Lu Jianying went upriver to Jiujiang, En was made wing commander and placed at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 與賊戰江中，毀賊船三十餘艘，眾寡不敵，死之。

translations.literal: He fought the rebels on the river, destroyed more than thirty rebel boats, but was outnumbered and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the rebels on the river and destroyed more than thirty of their boats, but was overwhelmed and killed.

sentences.zh: 贈提督，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡武壯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Regional Commander, granted a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry with an additional Cloud Cavalry commandant, and given the posthumous title Wuzhuang (Martial and Stalwart).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made regional commander, granted a hereditary cavalry command with an additional cloud-cavalry title, and honored with the posthumous name Martial and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 陳勝元，福建同安人。

translations.literal: Chen Shengyuan was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shengyuan was a native of Tong'an in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 由行伍歷官福建參將。

translations.literal: From the ranks he rose through office to brigade commander in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen from the ranks to brigade commander in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 捕洋盜有功，累擢江南福山鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He had merit in capturing foreign pirates and was promoted in succession to garrison commander of Fushan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself capturing foreign pirates and was eventually promoted to commander of the Fushan garrison in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 率水師防江，賊至太平四合山，迎擊，追至蕪湖，中砲落水，死之。

translations.literal: He led the naval forces to guard the river; when the rebels reached Sihe Mountain in Taiping he met them in battle, pursued them to Wuhu, was struck by cannon fire and fell into the water, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the river fleet on the Yangtze defense. When the rebels reached Sihe Mountain in Taiping he engaged them, pursued them as far as Wuhu, was struck by cannon fire, fell into the river, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 贈提督，予騎都尉世職，諡剛勇。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Regional Commander, granted a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry, and given the posthumous title Gangyong (Hard and Brave).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made regional commander, granted a hereditary commandant-of-cavalry title, and honored with the posthumous name Hard and Brave.

sentences.zh: 祁宿藻，字幼章，山西壽陽人，大學士俊藻弟也。

translations.literal: Qi Suzao, styled Youzhang, was a native of Shouyang in Shanxi and younger brother of Grand Secretary Qi Junzao.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Suzao, courtesy name Youzhang, was a native of Shouyang in Shanxi and the younger brother of Grand Secretary Qi Junzao.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he passed the jinshi examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 以召對受宣宗知，特簡授湖北黃州知府，調武昌。

translations.literal: Through an imperial audience he won the notice of the Xuanzong Emperor and was specially appointed prefect of Huangzhou in Hubei, then transferred to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial audience won him the favor of the Daoguang Emperor, who personally appointed him prefect of Huangzhou in Hubei and soon transferred him to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 連年大水，城幾沒，堵禦獲全。

translations.literal: For successive years great floods came; the city was nearly submerged, but by blocking and defending it was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year the floods rose until the city was nearly submerged, but by building dikes and organizing the defense he kept Wuchang intact.

sentences.zh: 治急賑，煮粥施錢及衣棺藥餌，全活災民甚眾，政聲最。

translations.literal: He managed emergency relief, distributing congee, money, clothing, coffins, and medicines, and saved a great many sufferers; his reputation in office was the highest.
translations.idiomatic: He organized emergency relief, distributing gruel, cash, clothing, coffins, and medicine, and saved a great many lives. His reputation as an official was unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 超擢廣東鹽運使，遷按察使，又遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted out of turn to Guangdong Salt Transport Commissioner, then transferred to provincial judge, and again to Hunan provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted ahead of schedule to Guangdong salt transport commissioner, then made provincial judge, and later provincial administration commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 會韶州數縣土匪起，詔留宿藻督兵往剿，七戰皆捷，匪首就擒。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in several counties of Shaozhou, an edict kept Suzao in office to lead troops to suppress them; in seven battles he was victorious each time and the bandit chiefs were captured.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in several counties around Shaozhou, the throne ordered Suzao to remain in office and lead troops against them. He won seven engagements in a row and captured the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 事平，賜花翎。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 調江寧布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangning as provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Nanjing as provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，河決豐北，山東、江北皆被水。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng the Yellow River burst its banks at Fengbei; Shandong and the north of the Jiang were inundated.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 the Yellow River burst its banks at Fengbei, flooding Shandong and the country north of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 大學士杜受田奉命臨賑，疏請以宿藻督辦江北賑務，章程出其手定，奏頒兩省行之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Du Shoutian was ordered to oversee relief on the spot; he memorialized asking that Suzao supervise relief north of the Jiang; the regulations were drawn up by his own hand and, once memorialized and approved, were put into effect in both provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Du Shoutian was sent to supervise relief on the spot and memorialized that Suzao be put in charge of relief north of the Yangtze. Suzao drafted the regulations himself, and after imperial approval they were implemented in both provinces.

sentences.zh: 及粵匪將東下，宿藻馳返江寧，括庫儲治軍械，盡移兵糈及南門外商市囤米入城，號召義勇之士備戰守。

translations.literal: When the Cantonese rebels were about to march east, Suzao hurried back to Jiangning, drew on the treasury stores to prepare arms, moved all military grain and the hoarded rice of the foreign merchants' quarter south of the city gate into the city, and called up volunteer fighters to prepare for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were about to march east down the Yangtze, Suzao raced back to Nanjing, drew on the treasury to arm the garrison, moved all military grain and the rice hoarded by foreign merchants south of the South Gate into the city, and rallied volunteers for the defense.

sentences.zh: 見督撫倉皇失措，各存意見，勸諫不聽，乃偕祥厚等密疏上聞。

translations.literal: Seeing the governor-general and governor flustered and at odds with each other, he remonstrated in vain and then joined Xianghou and others in a secret memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the governor-general and governor panicked and at odds with each other, he urged them in vain to pull together and finally joined Xianghou and others in a secret memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 建瀛既被罪失眾心，宿藻獨任事，賊至，力疾登陴指揮，曆三晝夜，城大兵單，援師不至，知事不可為，在城上嘔血數升，卒。

translations.literal: After Jianying had been punished and lost the people's hearts, Suzao alone bore the burden of affairs; when the rebels came he forced himself, though ill, onto the ramparts to direct operations for three days and nights; the city was large and the troops few, relief did not arrive, he knew the cause was lost, vomited several sheng of blood on the wall, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianying was punished and lost all authority, Suzao alone shouldered the work of defense. When the rebels arrived he dragged himself, though ill, onto the ramparts and directed the fighting for three days and nights. The city was vast and the garrison thin; no relief came. Seeing that all was lost, he vomited blood on the wall and died.

sentences.zh: 文宗悼惜，加等優血卩，贈右都御史，廕一子以知州用。

translations.literal: The Wenzong Emperor grieved; an augmented grade of preferential posthumous allowance was granted; he was posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief, and one son was given the privilege of appointment as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianfeng Emperor mourned his loss and granted enhanced posthumous honors. Suzao was posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief, and one son was given the privilege of appointment as prefect.

sentences.zh: 同治初，江南平，兄俊藻遣尋其遺櫬，得之城北僻地。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi, when Jiangnan was pacified, his elder brother Junzao sent men to search for his remains and found the coffin in a secluded place north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, after Jiangnan was pacified, his elder brother Junzao sent men to search for his remains and found the coffin in a secluded spot north of the city.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓以聞，請附祀祥厚專祠，追諡文節。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan reported this and requested that he be attached in worship at Xianghou's special shrine; he was given the posthumous title Wenjie (Cultured and Upright).
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan reported the find and asked that Suzao be worshipped in Xianghou's memorial shrine. He was posthumously honored with the name Cultured and Upright.

sentences.zh: 當城陷時，署布政使鹽巡道塗文鈞、江安糧道陳克讓、江寧知府魏亨逵、同知承恩、通判程文榮、上元知縣劉同纓、江寧知縣張行澍同死之。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Acting Provincial Administration Commissioner and Salt Circuit Intendant Tu Wenjun, Jiang'an Grain Transport Commissioner Chen Kerang, Jiangning Prefect Wei Hengkui, Subprefect Cheng En, Assistant Prefect Cheng Wenrong, Shangyuan County Magistrate Liu Tongying, and Jiangning County Magistrate Zhang Xingshu all died together.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Acting Commissioner Tu Wenjun, Grain Transport Commissioner Chen Kerang, Prefect Wei Hengkui, Subprefect Cheng En, Assistant Prefect Cheng Wenrong, Shangyuan magistrate Liu Tongying, and Jiangning magistrate Zhang Xingshu all died in the defense.

sentences.zh: 克讓，奉天承德人。

translations.literal: Kerang was a native of Chengde in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kerang was a native of Chengde in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 道光三年進士，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 累擢四川綏遠知府，調成都。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to prefect of Suiyuan in Sichuan and was transferred to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prefect of Suiyuan in Sichuan and was later transferred to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，擢江安糧道，居官清正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Jiang'an Grain Transport Commissioner; in office he was upright and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he was appointed Jiang'an grain transport commissioner and earned a reputation for integrity in office.

sentences.zh: 賊將至，或勸以督運出。

translations.literal: When the rebels were about to arrive, some urged him to supervise the transport of grain out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were approaching, some urged him to supervise the evacuation of grain stores from the city.

sentences.zh: 克讓曰：「江寧東南都會，失則大局危。

translations.literal: Kerang said: "Jiangning is the great metropolis of the southeast; if it is lost the whole strategic situation is endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Kerang replied: "Nanjing is the great metropolis of the southeast. If it falls, the whole strategic situation is lost.

sentences.zh: 去將焉往？

translations.literal: If I leave, where shall I go?"
translations.idiomatic: Where would I go if I fled?"

sentences.zh: 」又請徙其孥，其妻泣曰：「去為民望，不如死！

translations.literal: " He was again asked to move his family; his wife wept and said: "To leave would be to abandon the people's hope—better to die!"
translations.idiomatic: " When he was urged to send his family away, his wife wept and said, "If you leave, you abandon the people's hope. Better to die!"

sentences.zh: 」宿藻死而不瞑，克讓撫之曰：「庫尚有儲金，當​​募死士以成君志。

translations.literal: " When Suzao died with his eyes still open, Kerang stroked the body and said: "The treasury still holds reserve funds; we must recruit dare-to-die men to fulfill your purpose."
translations.idiomatic: " When Suzao died with his eyes still open, Kerang laid a hand on the body and said, "The treasury still holds reserve funds. We shall recruit die-hards to finish what you began."

sentences.zh: 」克讓守清涼山，督兵戰，殞於陣。

translations.literal: " Kerang held Qingliang Hill, directed the troops in battle, and fell on the field.
translations.idiomatic: " Kerang held Qingliang Hill, led the troops in battle, and was killed on the field.

sentences.zh: 弟克誠，子鬆恩，同遇害。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ke Cheng and his son Song'en were killed together with him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ke Cheng and his son Song'en were killed with him.

sentences.zh: 妻李，自經死。

translations.literal: His wife Li hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, née Li, hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 賜卹，予騎都尉世職，本籍請建專祠，追諡忠節。

translations.literal: Mourning grants were bestowed; he was given a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry; his home district requested a special shrine; he was given the posthumous title Zhongjie (Loyal and Upright).
translations.idiomatic: The court granted mourning honors and a hereditary commandant-of-cavalry title. His home district petitioned for a dedicated shrine, and he was posthumously honored as Loyal and Upright.

sentences.zh: 同纓，江西石城人。

translations.literal: Tongying was a native of Shicheng in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tongying was a native of Shicheng in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 拔貢。

translations.literal: He was a selected tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the provincial tribute-student examination.

sentences.zh: 歷官鹽城、泰興、江浦、上元、六合、江寧諸縣，皆有聲。

translations.literal: He served in succession as magistrate of Yancheng, Taixing, Jiangpu, Shangyuan, Luhe, and Jiangning, winning reputation at each post.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Yancheng, Taixing, Jiangpu, Shangyuan, Luhe, and Jiangning in turn, earning a fine reputation at every post.

sentences.zh: 江寧治防，儲糧練團，胥賴其力。

translations.literal: In Jiangning's preparations for defense, storing grain and drilling militia, all relied on his efforts.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's preparations for defense—stockpiling grain and drilling militia—depended largely on his efforts.

sentences.zh: 賊初至，假向榮書請入城，同纓察其詐，卻之。

translations.literal: When the rebels first arrived they forged a letter from Xiang Rong asking entry into the city; Tongying detected the fraud and refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels first arrived they forged a letter from Xiang Rong asking to be admitted into the city. Tongying saw through the ruse and refused.

sentences.zh: 砲裂城，率死士禦擊复完。

translations.literal: When cannon fire breached the wall, he led dare-to-die troops to repel the attack and restored the breach.
translations.idiomatic: When cannon fire breached the wall he led a band of die-hards in a counterattack and sealed the breach.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，賦絕命詞，投水死，卹典加等，贈道銜，諡武烈。

translations.literal: When the city fell he composed a death poem, threw himself into the water, and died; mourning honors were raised a grade, he was posthumously given the rank of circuit intendant, and given the posthumous title Wulie (Martial and Fierce).
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he wrote a final poem, threw himself into the water, and drowned. The court raised his mourning honors, posthumously granted him circuit-intendant rank, and honored him with the posthumous name Martial and Fierce.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌，字云閣，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Rui Chang, styled Yunge, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang, courtesy name Yunge, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 六世祖敖德，以軍功予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Aode was granted a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry for military merit.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Aode had been granted a hereditary commandant-of-cavalry title for military merit.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌由拜唐阿授鑾儀衛整儀尉，累遷冠軍使。

translations.literal: Rui Chang, from the rank of baitang'a, was appointed Ceremonial Guard orderly and was promoted in succession to Champion Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang entered service as a baitang'a and was appointed an orderly in the Imperial Procession Guard, rising in time to champion envoy.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年，擢正白旗漢軍副都統，歷金州、吉林副都統。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he was promoted to Han Chinese Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Plain White Banner and served as deputy commander at Jinzhou and Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 he was appointed Han Chinese deputy commander-in-chief of the Plain White Banner and served deputy commandancies at Jinzhou and Jilin.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，擢杭州將軍，未之任，率盛京兵赴淮、徐，專辦山東防剿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was promoted to General of Hangzhou but did not take up the post; he led Shengjing troops to Huai and Xu and was charged solely with defense and suppression in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1853 he was appointed general at Hangzhou but never took up the post. Instead he led troops from Mukden to the Huai and Xu region to organize defense and suppression in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 尋從僧格林沁、勝保勦賊畿輔。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed Senggelinqin and Sengbao in suppressing rebels in the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Senggelinqin and Sengbao in campaigns against the rebels in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 四年，連戰靜海、河間、東光。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he fought successive battles at Jinghai, Hejian, and Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854 he fought a series of engagements at Jinghai, Hejian, and Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 五年，會攻連鎮，扼河西，毀賊巢木城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he joined the assault on Lianzhen, held the west bank of the river, and destroyed the rebels' wooden fort.
translations.idiomatic: In 1855 he took part in the assault on Lianzhen, held the west bank of the river, and destroyed the rebels' wooden fort.

sentences.zh: 賊首林鳳祥就擒，被詔嘉獎，命赴本任。

translations.literal: When the rebel leader Lin Fengxiang was captured, he received an edict of commendation and was ordered to proceed to his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel leader Lin Fengxiang was captured, the throne commended him and ordered him to take up his post at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，粵匪由廣德入浙境，省城兵單，分防湖州、孝豐、餘杭。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year the Cantonese rebels entered Zhejiang from Guangde; troops in the provincial capital were few, and detachments were posted to defend Huzhou, Xiaofeng, and Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1860 the rebels entered Zhejiang from Guangde. Hangzhou's garrison was thin, and troops were posted to defend Huzhou, Xiaofeng, and Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 賊分股突犯杭州，瑞昌令副都統來存出武林門御之，自守錢塘門，偕巡撫羅遵殿佈置甫定，賊已麕至，縱火撲城。

translations.literal: Rebel columns suddenly struck Hangzhou; Rui Chang ordered Deputy Commander Laicun out through Wulin Gate to meet them while he himself held Qiantang Gate; he and Governor Luo Zundian had just finished their dispositions when the rebels swarmed in and set fires to storm the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel columns struck Hangzhou. Rui Chang sent Deputy Commander Laicun out through Wulin Gate to meet them while he held Qiantang Gate himself. He and Governor Luo Zundian had barely finished their dispositions when the rebels swarmed in and set fires along the walls.

sentences.zh: 越十日，地雷發，城陷。

translations.literal: After ten days a mine exploded and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later a mine blew open the wall and the outer city fell.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌率旗兵迎擊於湧金門，殺傷相當。

translations.literal: Rui Chang led the banner troops to meet the attack at Yongjin Gate; casualties on both sides were about equal.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang led the banner troops out at Yongjin Gate. Casualties on both sides were heavy.

sentences.zh: 退守駐防子城，賊屢攻，力拒卻之。

translations.literal: He withdrew to hold the garrison inner citadel; the rebels attacked repeatedly but were driven back with hard fighting.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew into the banner garrison quarter. The rebels attacked again and again, but each assault was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 相持六日，會張玉良率援兵至，夾擊，賊棄城走，遂復杭州，特詔嘉獎，賜黃馬褂，予二等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: The standoff lasted six days; then Zhang Yuliang arrived with relief troops, and in a pincer attack the rebels abandoned the city and fled; Hangzhou was recovered; a special edict commended him; he was granted the yellow riding jacket and a hereditary second-rank Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: After six days Zhang Yuliang arrived with relief troops. In a pincer attack the rebels abandoned the city and fled, and Hangzhou was recovered. The throne issued a special commendation, awarded him the yellow riding jacket, and granted a hereditary second-rank commandant-of-light-chariots title.

sentences.zh: 既而江南大營潰，常、蘇兩郡陷。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the great camp in Jiangnan collapsed and the prefectures of Changzhou and Suzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the great Jiangnan camp collapsed, and Changzhou and Suzhou were lost.

sentences.zh: 張玉良以罪黜，命瑞昌總統江南諸軍，江長貴副之，規復甦州，而賊已陷長興、武康，复諭先顧杭城，再圖進取。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang was dismissed for fault; Rui Chang was ordered to take overall command of the Jiangnan armies with Jiang Changgui as his deputy, with the plan of recovering Suzhou; but the rebels had already taken Changxing and Wukang, and he was again instructed to secure Hangzhou first and plan advances afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang was dismissed in disgrace. Rui Chang was placed in overall command of the Jiangnan armies with Jiang Changgui as his deputy, with orders to recover Suzhou. But the rebels had already taken Changxing and Wukang, and he was told to secure Hangzhou first and plan further advances later.

sentences.zh: 嘉興尋為賊踞，命瑞昌督張玉良往攻，亦未果。

translations.literal: Jiaxing was soon occupied by rebels; Rui Chang was ordered to direct Zhang Yuliang in an attack, but this too did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaxing soon fell to the rebels. Rui Chang was ordered to direct Zhang Yuliang in an assault on the city, but the attempt failed.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊陷富陽、餘杭，复撲杭州，瑞昌親督副都統傑純、副將吳再升擊走之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the rebels took Fuyang and Yuhang and again stormed Hangzhou; Rui Chang personally directed Deputy Commander Jie Chun and Brigadier Wu Zaisheng in driving them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels took Fuyang and Yuhang and struck at Hangzhou again. Rui Chang personally directed Deputy Commander Jie Chun and Brigadier Wu Zaisheng in driving them back.

sentences.zh: 十一年，賊勢益張，由嘉興進陷石門，湖州亦被圍，浙東諸郡相繼失守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year rebel strength grew greater; advancing from Jiaxing they took Shimen; Huzhou was also besieged, and the prefectures of eastern Zhejiang fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 the rebels grew stronger still. Advancing from Jiaxing they took Shimen and besieged Huzhou, while prefecture after prefecture in eastern Zhejiang fell.

sentences.zh: 自紹興為賊踞，杭州愈危，遂被圍，瑞昌偕巡撫王有齡嬰城固守逾兩月。

translations.literal: Once Shaoxing was held by rebels, Hangzhou grew still more perilous and was besieged; Rui Chang, with Governor Wang Youling, tied themselves to the city in a stubborn defense for more than two months.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shaoxing fell, Hangzhou grew still more desperate and was besieged. Rui Chang and Governor Wang Youling held the city in a desperate defense for more than two months.

sentences.zh: 張玉良戰城下，傷殞，軍心益渙。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuliang fought below the walls, was wounded and killed, and army morale grew still more shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuliang fought below the walls, was wounded and killed, and army morale collapsed further.

sentences.zh: 外援不至，糧道皆絕。

translations.literal: Relief did not arrive and all supply routes were cut.
translations.idiomatic: No relief came, and every supply route was cut.

sentences.zh: 瑞昌憂憤成疾，旗兵精壯多傷亡，乃集將校，誓死報國，家給火藥。

translations.literal: Rui Chang fell ill from grief and anger; many of the banner troops' best fighters had been killed or wounded; he then gathered his officers, swore to die for the state, and distributed gunpowder to every household.
translations.idiomatic: Rui Chang fell ill with grief and rage. Most of the banner garrison's best fighters were dead or wounded. He gathered his officers, swore to die for the dynasty, and distributed gunpowder to every household in the garrison.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，瑞昌先舉火自焚，闔營次第火起，同死者，杭州副都統關福及江蘇糧儲道赫特赫納以下男婦四千餘人。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Rui Chang was the first to set fire and burn himself; fires rose in succession throughout the camp; those who died with him included Hangzhou Deputy Commander Guan Fu and Jiangsu Grain Commissioner Hetehna, and more than four thousand men and women below them.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Rui Chang was the first to set himself ablaze. Fires rose one after another through the garrison quarter. More than four thousand men and women died with him, including Deputy Commander Guan Fu and Jiangsu grain commissioner Hetehna.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔優恤，贈太子太保，晉一等輕車都尉世職，諡忠壯。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict granted preferential mourning; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, his hereditary rank was raised to first-class Commandant of Light Chariots, and he was given the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict granted enhanced posthumous honors. Rui Chang was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, his hereditary rank was raised to first-class commandant of light chariots, and he was honored with the posthumous name Loyal and Stalwart.

sentences.zh: 入祀京師昭忠祠，杭州建專祠，死事者附祀焉。

translations.literal: He was entered in the Zhaozhong Shrine in the capital; a special shrine was built for him at Hangzhou, and those who died in the same cause were attached in worship.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the Zhaozhong Memorial Hall in Beijing, and a dedicated shrine was built for him at Hangzhou, with others who died in the defense worshipped there as well.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，杭州复，左宗棠奏瑞昌妾吳，於城破時挈兩幼子緒成、緒恩出走失散。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, when Hangzhou was recovered, Zuo Zongtang memorialized that Rui Chang's concubine Wu, when the city fell, had fled with two young sons Xucheng and Xu'en and been separated from them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, after Hangzhou was recovered, Zuo Zongtang reported that Rui Chang's concubine Wu had fled the fallen city with two young sons, Xucheng and Xu'en, and been separated from them in the chaos.

sentences.zh: 事定，尋得緒恩，護送回京。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, Xu'en was found and escorted back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, Xu'en was found and escorted back to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 詔念瑞昌忠烈，命本旗傳交其長子內閣中書緒光收養，飭宗棠購訪緒成下落，迄未得。

translations.literal: An edict, recalling Rui Chang's loyal martyrdom, ordered his banner to hand the boy over to his eldest son, Secretariat Drafter Xuguang, for adoption, and instructed Zongtang to search out Xucheng's whereabouts; he was never found.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by Rui Chang's martyrdom, the throne ordered his banner to place the boy in the care of his eldest son, Secretariat drafter Xuguang, and instructed Zuo Zongtang to search for Xucheng. He was never found.

sentences.zh: 後以兩世職並為三等子爵。

translations.literal: Later the two hereditary offices were combined into a third-rank baronage.
translations.idiomatic: Later the two hereditary offices were combined into a third-rank baronage.

sentences.zh: 傑純，布庫魯氏，蒙古正白旗人，杭州駐防。

translations.literal: Jie Chun, of the Bukuru clan, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner, garrisoned at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Chun, of the Bukuru clan, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner stationed at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 由驍騎校累遷協領。

translations.literal: From captain of the vanguard cavalry he was promoted in succession to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen from captain of the vanguard cavalry to company commander.

sentences.zh: 忠勇得士心，為瑞昌所倚。

translations.literal: Loyal and brave, he won the soldiers' hearts and was relied on by Rui Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and loyal, he won the soldiers' devotion and became Rui Chang's right hand.

sentences.zh: 杭州初破，瑞昌欲自剄，傑純與副都統來存言賊以偏師疾至，未有後繼，猶可力保駐防城以待外援，瑞昌從之，乃登陴守禦。

translations.literal: When Hangzhou was first breached, Rui Chang wished to cut his own throat; Jie Chun and Deputy Commander Laicun said the rebels had come with only a detached force in haste and had no follow-up troops, and that the garrison quarter could still be held hard until outside relief came; Rui Chang assented and mounted the ramparts to defend.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou first fell, Rui Chang meant to take his own life. Jie Chun and Deputy Commander Laicun urged that the rebels had arrived with only a vanguard and no reserves, and that the garrison quarter could still be held until relief came. Rui Chang agreed and took to the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 傑純當武林門，日與賊戰，長子前鋒校納蘇鏗陣亡，不之顧，殮其屍，不哭，曰：「汝先得所歸矣！

translations.literal: Jie Chun held Wulin Gate and fought the rebels day after day; his eldest son, vanguard captain Nasu Keng, fell on the field; he paid no heed, laid out the body, and did not weep, saying: "You have found your place first!"
translations.idiomatic: Jie Chun held Wulin Gate and fought the rebels day after day. His eldest son, vanguard captain Nasu Keng, was killed in action. He gave no sign of grief, laid out the body, and said without weeping, "You have found your rest before me!"

sentences.zh: 」及援兵至，怒馬突出，賊披靡，追擊出城十里外。

translations.literal: " When relief troops arrived, he spurred his horse out in fury; the rebels broke and fled, and he pursued them more than ten li beyond the city.
translations.idiomatic: " When relief arrived he charged out on a furious horse. The rebels broke and fled, and he pursued them more than ten li beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 以復城功，賜花翎。

translations.literal: For merit in recovering the city he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in recovering the city he was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 擢寧夏副都統，留浙協同團練大臣統率練勇，出省复富陽。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Deputy Commander of Ningxia but remained in Zhejiang to assist the militia commissioner in commanding trained braves and led troops out of the province to recover Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander at Ningxia but remained in Zhejiang to assist the militia commissioner in commanding local forces, and led troops out to recover Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，賊复犯杭州，迎剿於觀音橋，手刃數賊，率西湖水勇截擊，斬馘甚眾，又連破撲城之賊，追至留下，進克餘杭，賜號額騰伊巴圖魯。

translations.literal: That winter the rebels again attacked Hangzhou; he met them at Guanyin Bridge, killed several rebels with his own hand, led West Lake water braves in an intercepting attack and took many heads, broke successive assaults on the walls, pursued as far as Liuxia, advanced and recovered Yuhang, and was granted the title Eteng Ilbatu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebels struck at Hangzhou again. He met them at Guanyin Bridge, killed several with his own blade, and led West Lake boatmen in an ambush that took many heads. He broke repeated assaults on the walls, pursued the enemy to Liuxia, and recaptured Yuhang. The throne granted him the honorific title Eteng Ilbatu.

sentences.zh: 調授乍浦副都統，仍留防省城。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Deputy Commander of Zhapu but still remained to defend the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed deputy commander at Zhapu but remained to defend the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 十一年，城再陷，傑純戰一晝夜，所部傷亡略盡，遣次子出避，以存宗祀，闔門自焚，獨策馬入賊陣，死之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the city fell again; Jie Chun fought for a day and a night until his command was nearly wiped out; he sent his second son away to preserve the family line, his whole household burned themselves, and he alone spurred his horse into the rebel ranks and died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 the city fell again. Jie Chun fought for a day and a night until his command was nearly destroyed. He sent his second son away to preserve the family line, his household set themselves ablaze, and he alone rode into the rebel ranks and was killed.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其一門忠烈，依都統例賜卹，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，杭州、乍浦並建專祠，子婦孫僕皆附祀。

translations.literal: An edict praised the loyal martyrdom of his whole household; mourning was granted on the commander-in-chief precedent; he was given a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry with an additional Cloud Cavalry commandant; special shrines were built at both Hangzhou and Zhapu, and sons, daughters-in-law, grandchildren, and servants were all attached in worship.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended the martyrdom of his entire household, granted mourning honors on the commander-in-chief precedent, and awarded a hereditary cavalry command with an additional cloud-cavalry title. Dedicated shrines were built at Hangzhou and Zhapu, with sons, daughters-in-law, grandchildren, and servants all worshipped there.

sentences.zh: 後復加恩入祀京師昭忠祠，諡果毅。

translations.literal: Later further grace was shown by entry in the Zhaozhong Shrine in the capital, and he was given the posthumous title Guoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was further honored with a place in the Zhaozhong Memorial Hall in Beijing and the posthumous name Resolute.

sentences.zh: 擢次子固魯鏗知府，改歸京旗。

translations.literal: His second son Gulu Keng was promoted to prefect and transferred back to the capital banner.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Gulu Keng was promoted to prefect and transferred back to the capital banner.

sentences.zh: 錫齡阿，扎哈蘇氏，蒙古正白旗人，荊州駐防。

translations.literal: Xi Ling'a, of the Zhahasu clan, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner, garrisoned at Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Ling'a, of the Zhahasu clan, was a Mongol of the Plain White Banner stationed at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以佐領率兵從戰沔陽、監利、潛江、應城、漢陽、宜昌。

translations.literal: As assistant company commander he led troops in campaigns at Mianyang, Jianli, Qianjiang, Yingcheng, Hanyang, and Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant company commander he led troops in campaigns at Mianyang, Jianli, Qianjiang, Yingcheng, Hanyang, and Yichang.

sentences.zh: 積功累擢福州副都統，調乍浦副都統。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was promoted in succession to Deputy Commander of Fuzhou and transferred to Deputy Commander of Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he was promoted to deputy commander at Fuzhou and later transferred to Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 十一年，賊來犯，督兵出戰，城中內應起，折回巷戰，全軍皆沒，與兩子榮輝、榮耀同殞於陣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year rebels came to attack; he led troops out to fight; collaborators rose inside the city; he turned back to fight in the lanes; the whole force was wiped out, and he perished on the field together with his two sons Ronghui and Rongyao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1861 the rebels attacked. He led his troops out to meet them, but collaborators rose inside the city. He turned back to fight street by street until his whole force was destroyed. He and his two sons Ronghui and Rongyao were killed on the field.

sentences.zh: 贈都統銜，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，諡武烈，入祀京師昭忠祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the rank of Commander-in-Chief, granted a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry with an additional Cloud Cavalry commandant, given the posthumous title Wulie, and entered in the Zhaozhong Shrine in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted commander-in-chief rank, a hereditary cavalry command with an additional cloud-cavalry title, and the posthumous name Martial and Fierce, and was enshrined in the Zhaozhong Memorial Hall in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 嗣以荊州紳民感念保境功，請建專祠。

translations.literal: Later the gentry and people of Jingzhou, moved by gratitude for his merit in defending the territory, requested a special shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Later the gentry and people of Jingzhou, grateful for his defense of the region, petitioned for a dedicated shrine.

sentences.zh: 子榮輝、榮耀並予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: His sons Ronghui and Rongyao were both granted hereditary Cloud Cavalry commandant titles.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Ronghui and Rongyao were both granted hereditary cloud-cavalry titles.

sentences.zh: 論曰：清製，行省要區置旗兵駐防，其尤重都會，兵額多者，以將軍領之。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Under Qing institutions, banner troops were garrisoned in strategic areas of provinces; where the great metropolises were especially important and troop quotas were large, a general was placed in command.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Under the Qing system, banner garrisons were posted in the strategic districts of each province. In the greatest cities, where troop quotas were largest, a general was placed in command.

sentences.zh: 蓋監製疆臣，備不虞也。

translations.literal: This was to oversee and restrain frontier officials and guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: The purpose was to keep provincial officials in check and guard against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 承平恬嬉，非復國初勁旅，小有變動，可資鎮懾；

translations.literal: In long peace they grew indolent and complacent and were no longer the crack troops of the dynasty's founding; for small disturbances they could still serve to overawe;
translations.idiomatic: In long peace they grew soft and complacent and were no longer the crack troops of the founding era. For minor disturbances they could still serve as a deterrent;

sentences.zh: 鉅寇燎原，力不足以御之。

translations.literal: when a great rebel blaze spread across the land, their strength was not enough to withstand it.
translations.idiomatic: but when rebellion blazed across the empire, their strength was not enough to hold it back.

sentences.zh: 江南之失，誤於陸建瀛不預設防。

translations.literal: The loss of Jiangnan was due to Lu Jianying's failure to prepare defenses in advance.
translations.idiomatic: The loss of Jiangnan was due to Lu Jianying's failure to prepare defenses in advance.

sentences.zh: 祥厚倉猝專任，以孤城當方張之寇，寧有幸焉。

translations.literal: Xianghou, thrust suddenly into sole responsibility, with a lone city to face a rebel force at the height of its power—how could he have had any hope of success?
translations.idiomatic: Xianghou, thrust suddenly into sole command with a lone city against a rebel army at the height of its power, could hardly have hoped to succeed.

sentences.zh: 杭州初陷，賊僅偏師，故瑞昌能守內城以待援；

translations.literal: When Hangzhou first fell, the rebels were only a detached column, so Rui Chang could hold the inner city and await relief;
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou first fell, the rebels had sent only a vanguard, so Rui Chang could hold the inner quarter and wait for relief;

sentences.zh: 及蘇、常既失，輔車無依，終不能保，大勢然也。

translations.literal: but once Suzhou and Changzhou were lost and he had no supporting state to rely on, he could not be preserved in the end—the great trend was such.
translations.idiomatic: but once Suzhou and Changzhou were lost and he had no supporting territories to rely on, the city could not be saved. That was the force of circumstances.

sentences.zh: 然二人者，皆能以忠義激勵，城亡與亡，婦嬰皆知效死，烈已！

translations.literal: Yet these two men were both able to rouse others through loyalty and righteousness; when the city perished they perished with it; women and children alike knew how to die for the cause—how fierce their devotion!
translations.idiomatic: Yet both men roused others by their loyalty and courage. When their cities fell they fell with them, and even women and children knew how to die for the cause. How fierce their devotion was!

sentences.zh: 祁宿藻孤忠盡瘁，傑純智勇能軍，並一時傑出之才。

translations.literal: Qi Suzao, loyal to the end in solitary devotion; Jie Chun, wise and brave and able to command troops—both were outstanding talents of their age.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Suzao gave his life in solitary devotion to the throne. Jie Chun was wise, brave, and skilled in command. Both were outstanding men of their time.

sentences.zh: 炎岡同燼，世尤惜之。

translations.literal: Flames consumed the ridge together; the age especially mourns their loss.
translations.idiomatic: They perished together in the same blaze, and the age mourns them all the more.
